did_you_know.text: Did you know? This chapter says that Solomon married many women from various nations, including Moab, Ammon, Edom, Sidon, and the Hittites, in addition to Pharaoh’s daughter.
Did you know? According to the text, Solomon had 700 wives, who were princesses, and 300 concubines—a total of 1,000 women.
Did you know? In Solomon’s old age, his wives turned his heart toward other gods, so his heart was not fully devoted to the LORD his God as the heart of his father David had been.
Did you know? The LORD became angry with Solomon, even though the LORD had appeared to him twice and had commanded him not to follow other gods.
Did you know? The decree to tear the kingdom apart was postponed until the days of Solomon’s son, and the house of David retained one tribe for David’s sake and for the sake of Jerusalem.
Did you know? After Solomon’s sin, the LORD raised up an adversary against him in the person of Hadad the Edomite; later in the chapter, Rezon son of Eliada is also mentioned as another adversary.
Did you know? Hadad the Edomite, who had found refuge and status in Egypt, eventually asked Pharaoh to release him so that he could return to his own country.

Did you know? Jeroboam son of Nebat is described as a man of valor, and Solomon appointed him over all the forced labor of the house of Joseph—that is, the tax and public-works labor of the tribes of Joseph.

Did you know? The prophet Ahijah tore a new garment into twelve pieces and told Jeroboam to take ten of them as a symbol that the kingdom would be torn apart and that ten tribes would be given to him.
Did you know? Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel for forty years. After his death, he was buried in the City of David, and his son Rehoboam succeeded him as king.
